// Deliberately weak by construction: this page is static, so the app and every
// asset behind it can be fetched directly regardless of what this check says.
// It keeps casual visitors out. It is not access control, and nothing sensitive
// should ever sit behind it.
async function sha256(s) {
  const b = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(s));
  return [...new Uint8Array(b)].map(x => x.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')).join('');
}
const GATE_HASH = '2acd6e0d5f19f1589b4ff8af77e9f5a3e51ad2e8e78eda5055a4064b2f301e9f';
async function checkGate() {
  const v = document.getElementById('gate-pw').value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (await sha256(v) === GATE_HASH) {
    sessionStorage.setItem('arcs-gate', '1');
    document.getElementById('gate').style.display = 'none';
    document.getElementById('gated-content').style.display = 'block';
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));
  } else {
    document.getElementById('gate-err').textContent = 'Not quite — try again.';
  }
}
if (sessionStorage.getItem('arcs-gate') === '1') {
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
    document.getElementById('gate').style.display = 'none';
    document.getElementById('gated-content').style.display = 'block';
  });
}
</script>

<div id="gated-content">

## Citation arcs

Put in your ORCID, or search your name. It draws three views of your citation record: cumulative in
calendar time, cumulative aligned on each paper's publication year, and the per-year arc that shows
when your papers actually peaked. Venues are tiered against journals in your own topic area, so it
works outside political science too.

Everything runs **in your browser**. Your identifier goes to [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org) and
nowhere else — there is no server of mine involved and nothing is logged. The first load pulls down
R compiled to WebAssembly, so give it up to a minute.

Numbers will look low if you are used to Google Scholar. OpenAlex reports roughly two thirds of
Scholar's counts, because Scholar indexes preprints, chapters and theses that OpenAlex does not. It
ranks papers almost identically though, and these charts are about shape rather than level.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 720
#| components: [viewer]
{{< include ../posts/2026-08-citation-arcs/widget/app.R >}}
```

### Want the Google Scholar numbers instead?

The widget above uses OpenAlex, because Google Scholar has no API and blocks anything that isn't a
person sitting at a browser. If you want the Scholar counts you recognise — roughly 1.5× higher,
since Scholar indexes preprints, chapters and theses — you have to run it on your own machine. Two
minutes of setup.

In R (4.1 or newer):

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "DT", "dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "tibble",
                   "rlang", "ggplot2", "ggrepel", "scales", "jsonlite", "httr2"))

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("aserlich/scholar-arcs")

scholararcs::run_app(mailto = "you@example.edu")   # OpenAlex, same as above
```

For the Scholar backend, add one more package and pass `source`:

```r
install.packages("scholar")
scholararcs::run_app(source = "scholar")
```

Then paste your Scholar **profile id** — the `user=` value from your profile URL
(`scholar.google.com/citations?user=`**`h8n98PQAAAAJ`**). Name lookup isn't offered, because Google
no longer permits it.

Two things to expect. It fetches one paper at a time behind an 8-second throttle, so a 50-paper
profile takes around seven minutes; progress is cached as it goes, so if Google starts blocking you
can re-run and it resumes rather than starting over. And Scholar returns journal names but no venue
identifiers, so automatic tiering doesn't work on that backend — you group venues by hand, or load a
saved mapping.

Full instructions and the venue-grouping presets:
[**github.com/aserlich/scholar-arcs**](https://github.com/aserlich/scholar-arcs#use-google-scholar-instead)

### Tell me what's broken

Known weak spots, and the ones I'd most like reports on:

- **Venue tiering.** It ranks each journal against journals in your topic area by two-year mean
  citedness. Three reference populations were tried before one behaved. If it puts your journals
  somewhere absurd — especially in a field with different citation norms — that's the bug.
- **OpenAlex sometimes merges two researchers into one profile.** If someone else's career appears
  mixed into yours, that's why.
- **Small tiers give medians over one or two papers.** The charts draw them anyway.

Code: [github.com/aserlich/scholar-arcs](https://github.com/aserlich/scholar-arcs)
